summary: Enhance your skills in leveraging international aid for social protection programs with our comprehensive training course. Enroll now to make a difference!
lede: Leveraging international aid for social protection programs means matching funding and partnerships to program needs while supporting durable systems. This training is for government, NGO, development-agency and policy professionals who design, fund or deliver social protection. Participants learn to map donors and funding options, develop fundable program designs and proposals, and build financing, coordination, monitoring and risk-accountability frameworks.
audienceIntro: This course is tailored for professionals regularly engaging with donors, designing or implementing social protection programs, or influencing funding decisions. This course is designed for: Government officials in ministries of social protection, finance, planning, or labour. Social protection program managers and technical officers. NGO and civil society leaders running cash transfer, safety net, or livelihood support programs. Staff in development agencies, multilaterals, and bilateral donors who support social protection portfolios. Policy advisors and social development specialists working on poverty reduction and inclusion. Monitoring, evaluation, and learning professionals supporting donor-funded social protection. Finance and grants managers who structure and manage funding for social protection. Social policy researchers and analysts informing program design and funding strategies. Coordinators of social registries, targeting systems, and integrated social protection platforms. Anyone involved in negotiating, managing, or advocating for international aid to support social protection systems.
modules: Global Landscape of International Aid and Social Protection
Mapping Donors and Funding Opportunities for Social Protection
Building Strong Concept Notes and Funding Proposals
Financing and Partnership Models for Social Protection
Implementation, Coordination, and Governance of Aid-funded Programs
Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning for Donor-supported Social Protection
prerequisites: Participants should have experience in program management, policy making, or financial management within government, NGOs, or development agencies, and a basic understanding of social protection concepts.
